title: Bernoulli switching lemma for DNF formulas
statement:
Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n \ge 1$ Boolean variables whose width is at most $w$, where $w \ge 1$, and suppose that no term of $f$ reads any variable more than once: each term is a duplicate-free list of literals, and any two literals in a common term that share a variable are equal. Fix a real parameter $p$ with $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$, so in particular $p \le 1$. Then for every $t \in \bbn$, under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$ the restricted function $f\vert_\rho$ (that is, $f$ evaluated on the free coordinates with the remaining coordinates fixed by $\rho$) satisfies
\[
  \Pr_{p}\big[\, f\vert_\rho \text{ has decision-tree depth exceeding } t \,\big] \;\le\; \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right),
\]
where the decision-tree depth of a Boolean function is the least depth of a decision tree computing it.
hypotheses_covered: each term reads any shared variable identically (no conflicting literals)
each term has no duplicate literals
replaced:
Let $f$ be a width-$w$ DNF ($0 < w$) with no repeated variables per term, and
$0 < n$. For a Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction with $0 < p \le 1/(40w)$ and
$p \le 1$, and for every $t$,
\[
  \Pr_{R_p}\big[\mathrm{dtDepth}(f|_\rho) > t\big]
    \;\le\; \left(\tfrac12\right)^t + e^{-np/3}.
\]
The $(1/2)^t$ term comes from the switching lemma via the Bernoulli cost
reduction, and $e^{-np/3}$ is the Chernoff tail for leaving too many free
variables.
